hour_convention: hour h = the interval h:00 to h+1:00, local time (WAT, UTC+1)

appliances.name: DC refrigerator ~100 L, shiftable cooling (pre-cooling)
appliances.note: 30% of the fridge's night energy (97.5 Wh/day). The standard controller runs it in the evening; the smart controller moves it to midday (pre-cooling, the fridge's thermal mass stores the cold). Same energy in both cases, so the comparison is fair; in reality pre-cooling in the midday heat costs a little more (TO CONFIRM).

sources.fans: CLASP / Efficiency for Access, 2021 Appliance Data Trends: tested pedestal fans 14-34 W; efficient 12 V BLDC fan <= 15 W; about 9 h/day of use in hot seasons. 20 W chosen as a mid value.
sources.tv: CLASP / EforA Solar Appliance Technology Brief: Televisions (May 2021): most efficient 32-inch model 8 W, market 32-inch TVs 20-40 W. 20 W = efficient model sold in SHS bundles.
sources.fridge: CLASP / EforA Solar Appliance Technology Brief: Refrigerators (June 2021): median VeraSol-tested refrigerator 0.5 kWh/24h; field tests in Uganda found 80-124% above lab values for medium and large units. 0.6 kWh/day (+20%) chosen for Maiduguri heat, TO CONFIRM.
sources.lights_phones_radio: Typical solar home system ratings (3 W LED bulbs, 5 W phone charging, 3 W radio). Phone energy 10 Wh/day per phone. TO CONFIRM against a vendor datasheet.
sources.usage_hours: Assumed daily routine for a 5-person household in Maiduguri (sunset ~18:00, hot nights). TO CONFIRM; no field survey available.

fridge_note: Fridge = 0.6 kWh/day (25 W average), split into three entries so that the flexible part has as many allowed hours as usual hours and no energy is lost when it is moved.
